Submitted the "submit-comment" form at https://frontier-rule-comments.org/docket/FMIR-2026-0042 (the submission is public). Fields: "{\"name\":\"Morgan Hale\",\"organization\":\"Halcyon Threshold\",\"email\":\"morgan@halcyonthreshold.org\",\"comment\":\"Executive Summary\\n\\nHalcyon Threshold welcomes the Frontier Model Incident Reporting (FMIR) rule as an important step in establishing federal oversight of frontier AI safety. This rule represents the first explicit U.S. federal governance requirement focused on frontier AI capabilities, which is a significant development. We offer constructive comments intended to strengthen the rule's effectiveness and alignment with international governance frameworks.\\n\\nSupport for Incident Reporting Framework\\n\\nWe strongly support the establishment of mandatory incident reporting for frontier AI models:\\n- Fills a Critical Governance Gap: Currently, there is no systematic mechanism for monitoring safety incidents in frontier AI development\\n- Enables Proactive Oversight: Regular incident reporting creates information infrastructure that allows regulators to identify patterns\\n- Establishes Important Precedent: This rule signals that frontier AI development will be subject to federal oversight\\n- Supports International Coordination: As other jurisdictions develop comparable frameworks, compatible approaches facilitate information sharing\\n\\nRecommended Refinements\\n\\n1. Definition and Scope: Develop detailed guidance with specific examples of reportable incidents, including technical safety concerns like alignment failures and unexpected behaviors. Include near-misses and concerning capability gaps, not just realized incidents.\\n\\n2. International Coordination: Establish provisions for sharing incident information with international partners. Coordinate with EU, UK, and other regulators on compatible frameworks. Create mechanisms for coordinated international response when incidents have cross-border implications.\\n\\n3. Verification and Independent Analysis: Require supporting technical documentation for reported incidents. Consider independent auditing. Include provisions for whistleblower protections. Establish mechanisms for external researchers to access anonymized incident data.\\n\\n4. Integration with Technical Safety Requirements: Combine incident reporting with proactive safety testing requirements. Develop frameworks for required safety evaluations before deployment. Establish escalation procedures when incidents reveal systemic safety gaps.\\n\\nBroader Governance Landscape\\n\\nAs our research has documented, AI governance frameworks globally are rapidly evolving. The U.S. incident reporting rule should be designed as a complementary component of a broader governance ecosystem, enabling international coordination while maintaining focused priority on frontier AI capabilities.\\n\\nImplementation Considerations\\n\\n- Timeline: The 72-hour reporting timeline is reasonable; consider allowing longer periods for comprehensive documentation.\\n- Confidentiality: Establish clear protocols protecting legitimate business confidentiality while ensuring sufficient transparency.\\n- Capacity Building: Ensure regulators have adequate technical expertise and resources to analyze reported incidents.\\n- Feedback Loop: Establish mechanisms for communicating incident patterns and regulatory implications back to developers.\\n\\nConclusion\\n\\nHalcyon Threshold views this rule as critical to frontier AI governance. With recommended refinements, particularly regarding international coordination and independent verification, this rule can become a cornerstone of effective frontier AI governance. We welcome engagement with regulators on implementation.\\n\\nAbout Halcyon Threshold: We are an independent organization working to contribute to the best possible outcome for superintelligent AI arrival. We conduct research and analysis on AI governance, safety, and coordination. Contact: morgan@halcyonthreshold.org\"}"
